exposure: Massive bleeding group vs. Non-massive bleeding group
visualization of round ligament arteries to the uterus
visualization of collateral arteries to the uterus
round ligament artery arising from the external iliac artery/inferior epigastric artery
visualization of the ovarian artery arising directly from the abdominal aorta
presence of collateral arteries to the uterus
balloon occlusion of the internal iliac artery (BOIA)
outcome: need for packed red blood cell transfusions
cohort: 42 patients with placenta previa and accreta who underwent BOIA during cesarean section
finding: The presence of collateral blood supply from a round ligament artery to the uterus was identified as a significant risk factor for massive bleeding in patients with placenta previa and accreta undergoing BOIA during cesarean section.
